messages:
zoe: Noticed a fresh wave of quota fragmentation this morning. Console shows duplicate lines for the same customer across routes. Traces point to varying client-side attribution shapes.
mark: Which shapes exactly?
zoe: Examples in logs: `X-Redwood-Meta: acct=team-echo` vs JSON `X-Redwood-Meta: {\"acct\":\"team-echo\",\"route\":\"beta\"}` vs legacy `acct_key=team-echo`.
li: We keep having the same conversation. I want a durable solution that doesn't rely on fragile header-name matching. What about the signed-attr approach we discussed last quarter?
mark: I like it. Quick recap: SDKs emit a small deterministic signature header that encodes acct+route (HMAC with version prefix). Ingest validates signature and uses it to coalesce console/telemetry buckets. Billing pipeline still uses raw headers so we keep auditability.
zoe: Agreed. Proposal additions: 1) versioned sigs (v1/v2) so we can rotate schemes; 2) sigs are short (base64url of 8 bytes) to avoid perf; 3) public verification key cached by ingest or use KMS HMAC verify.
li: Also add a fallback: if sig missing, ingestion falls back to deterministic parsing heuristics (acct match + route absent rule) and mark the record "heuristic_coalesce". Console shows whether a line is from sig or heuristic.
mark: SDK implementation notes: TS & Py will ship middleware lib that computes sig when acct available. Go will try to compute sig from token claims cheaply. All emissions behind env flag REDWOOD_EMIT_ATTR_SIG=0 -> flip to 1 in canary.
zoe: Security note: signing key must be per-region and rotated. We'll store HMAC keys in KMS and rotate via key version header: `X-Redwood-Attr-Sig: v1:kid:base64url`. Ingestion will map kid->key via KMS and cache for 1h. If verification fails, ingestion increments `ingest.attr_sig.verify_fail`.
li: Testing: add unit tests in SDKs for deterministic sig across language implementations (test vectors). Also E2E synthetic that sends mixed header shapes with sig present/absent.
mark: Console UX: add "coalesced (sig)" pill in quota charts and a drilldown to show underlying raw keys. Add an "adoption" metric card that breaks down sig adoption by SDK (ts/py/go) and region.
zoe: For rollout: canary ingest coalescer 6h @ 10% traffic, synthetic suite must validate: coalesced viz == sum(raw) and billing unchanged. If anomaly (more than 0.1% mismatch) -> rollback.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: 2026-08-02T03:00Z, pipeline #10723, stages: 10% -> 50% -> 100% on success.
li: Migration tooling: we should publish `rw-attr-check` CLI (python) that curls a customer endpoint and verifies emitted headers + sig. Provide example: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" https://api.redwood.ai/generate -v
# check response headers for X-Redwood-Attr-Sig

We can also add a small github action customers can run to validate.
mark: SDK PR plan: TS PR includes middleware + unit tests + test vectors. Py PR includes same and the CLI helper. Go PR adds lightweight sig path reading token claim. All PRs default with REDWOOD_EMIT_ATTR_SIG=0.
zoe: I'll draft the ingest coalescer and console tile prototype. Li, can you coordinate with security on KMS key lifecycle and rotation policy?
li: On it. I'll propose key rotation every 30 days with tooling to re-encrypt and publish new kid. Also will prepare a threat model doc for sig header abuse.
mark: I'll write SDK test vectors and start the TS PR tonight. Draft PR link when ready.
zoe: Action items: Zoe (ingest coalescer + console tile wireframe), Mark (TS PR + test vectors), Li (KMS & security), Py owner (middleware + CLI), Go owner (shim). We'll reconvene after canary.
mark: PR opened (draft): https://github.com/redwood/sdk-ts/pull/601 (middleware + deterministic sig tests).
li: Filing key rotation RFC today.
zoe: Good. Let's keep opt-in canary for 48h before flipping. Follow-up in #devex-standup tomorrow.
